definitions.text: Pedicle width was defined as the shortest distance along the perpendicular to the line through the axis of the pedicle (Fig. 1). Pedicle diameter was measured on axial slices through the thinnest portion of the pedicle using reformatted slices closest to the middle of the pedicle in the craniocaudad dimension. Outer cortex versus inner canal is not stated.

Pedicle parameters in patients and controls; columns: Level | PWc (mm) | PWv (mm) | PWn (mm) | PLc (mm) | PLv (mm) | PLn (mm). PWc = pedicle width on the concave side; PWv = pedicle width on the convex side; PWn = pedicle width in controls; PLc = pedicle length on the concave side; PLv = pedicle length on the convex side; PLn = pedicle length in controls; *p < 0.05 versus PWn (PLn) group; †p < 0.05 versus PWv (PLv) group.
Transverse pedicle width: the narrowest width of the pedicle in the transverse plane, measured outer cortex to outer cortex on CT scans for ease and reproducibility.

Twenty-four AIS patients, curves <100°, 14 female and 10 male; mean age 14.6 years (12.3–18.3), mean Cobb 76° (58–98°); King II 12, King III 7, King IV 5. [own inference] Convex is read as right and concave as left because all 24 patients had right thoracic/thoracolumbar curves; the paper does not explicitly equate convex with right.

Tables 1–3 explicitly label means, ranges, SD and number of pedicles separately. The printed field preserves the literal mean column; decimals records its printed decimal places. Table 4 conflicts are kept separately and are not used; Tables 1–3 supply primary figures. Doubtful cells remain usable as printed, while the impossible L4 convex angle is retained only for inspection.

definitions.text: Figure 1 defines transverse diameter as “the medial-lateral inner and outer cortical width of the pedicle” measured at the isthmus. Three measurements per parameter at the isthmus were averaged. Table 1 does not label which of its two rows is inner or outer: assigning the first row as inner and second as outer is this project’s own inference. The paper does not define the ± statistic; interpreting it as SD is this project’s own inference. The paper states a total of 120 children aged 5–14, selected by stratified random sampling; per-age-band and sex counts are not stated.

definitions.text: Measured by "cutting out pedicles in a plane perpendicular to the pedicle axis through the isthmus". Fig. 1 names W cortical pedicle width and w cancellous pedicle width; the discussion treats W as the outer diameter. Right pedicle is always convex; left pedicle is always concave. H is cortical pedicle height and h cancellous pedicle height. Per-cell n is not supplied.
Pedicle diameter: "the widest outer cortical diameter at the narrowest part of the pedicle". The full-paper abstract gives no per-level diameters; it does not fill anatomy cells.
